Understanding stock movement

Stock that sits on shelves costs money. Here is how to measure how fast it moves.

The formula

The inventory turnover ratio is the cost of goods sold divided by average inventory for the period.

Example

A shop with 300,000 cost of goods sold and 60,000 average inventory has a ratio of 5.

Accounts payable turnover: formula and example

Accounts payable turnover measures how many times a business pays off its suppliers in a period.

Formula

Accounts payable turnover is total supplier purchases divided by average accounts payable.

Worked example

Purchases of 500,000 and average payables of 50,000 give a turnover of 10.

What a high or low number means

A high number means suppliers are paid quickly; a low one can mean cash is tight.

Profitability basics

Profit tells you whether the business works.

The gross margin formula

Gross margin is revenue minus cost of goods sold, divided by revenue.

Example

Revenue of 200,000 and cost of goods sold of 120,000 give a gross margin of 40%.
